brief:
Four imprisoned Palestine Action activists have launched appeals against their terrorism-related sentences, according to Al Jazeera English. The convictions stem from their participation in a raid on an Israeli weapons manufacturer. Supporters of the activists contend the sentences establish a troubling precedent for protest activities targeting Israeli arms producers and argue that applying terrorism charges to the defendants' actions represents an overreach of the law.

The appeals challenge both the length of the sentences imposed and the legal framework used to prosecute the case. Advocates maintain the convictions could have chilling effects on legitimate demonstrations and civil disobedience campaigns directed at military equipment suppliers.
dek: Supporters of those who participated in a raid on an Israeli weapons maker say the sentences set a dangerous precedent.
title: Four Palestine Action activists appeal terrorism convictions
